about: The eight onboarding questions, exactly the eight answers in .claude/skills/onboard-brand/SKILL.md Step 1, in the same order (ONBOARDING-SPEC.md 14.1). 'Brand basics N of 8' counts these and nothing else. Examples describe the KIND of answer the made-up bakery gave; they are never a sentence to copy and never pre-fill a box. An answer that reads like its example is questioned before it can be confirmed.

questions.ask: What's your brand called, exactly as people say it?
questions.do: Type the name, then check the spelling and tap Spelled right.
questions.example: The bakery gave its name the way it's written on the shop sign, including the ampersand.

questions.ask: What do you do, and for whom?
questions.do: One or two sentences, the way you'd tell a friend.
questions.example: What they bake, the town they're in, and their weekend classes for home bakers.
questions.example_text: A neighbourhood sourdough bakery in a small river town. We bake naturally leavened bread every morning and teach weekend baking classes for home bakers.

questions.ask: Who are you trying to reach, and what's in their way?
questions.do: Describe them, then add three or four real questions they ask you.
questions.example: Home bakers whose loaves come out flat, and the exact questions those bakers ask at the counter.
questions.example_text: Home bakers who want better bread but keep getting dense, flat loaves.

questions.ask: Who speaks in your posts: you, the company, or both?
questions.do: Tap one, then check every name and handle.
questions.example: A person (the head baker, by name, with her role) and the company account.

questions.ask: Paste or type a few things you've really written or said.
questions.do: Posts, emails to customers, a transcript. Don't tidy them: they are saved word for word.

questions.ask: Your background, your main text, and the one colour people remember you by.
questions.do: Tap each colour to check or change it.
questions.example: A light background, a dark text colour that is easy to read on it, and one bright accent.

questions.ask: Any rules your posts must follow?
questions.do: Regulated industry, claims you must never make, who signs off, anyone never to name, words you hate.
questions.example: A bakery has no regulator, but it might never name its suppliers and hate the word “artisanal”.

questions.ask: What do you want the Social Media Factory to make?
questions.do: Tap any. Costs are explained later, before anything is signed up for.
questions.example: The bakery picked written posts and carousels to start.
